sentences.text:
This Miscellaneous First Appeal coming on for Final Hearing through Physical Hearing/Video Conferencing, this day,
the Court delivered the following:
JUDGMENT

The present appeal is filed by the claimant under Section 173 (1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988,
seeking enhancement of the compensation awarded by the Court of the learned Senior Civil Judge and Motor Accident Claims Tribunal at Holenarasipur, (hereinafter for brevity referred to as "the Tribunal"), in its judgment and award dated 30-03-2019, in M.V.C.No.578/2016.
2.

entities.text: Senior Civil Judge and Motor Accident Claims Tribunal at Holenarasipur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
The summary of the case of the claimant before the Tribunal was that, on the date 28-08-2015, at about 8:15 a.m., while he was going on his Motor Cycle bearing registration No.KA-13/ED-6602, on Hassan-Holenarasipura road, in front of Namratha Hitech Nursery, Kittane Gadi on the said road,
the driver of the KSRTC Bus bearing registration No.KA-13/F-2145, having driven the Bus in a rash and negligent manner, at a high speed, dashed to the claimant's Motor Cycle, due to which road traffic accident, the claimant sustained multiple injuries to his left shoulder, left forehead, left cheek,
left eye, chest and sustained fracture injury to his left hand.

He was immediately taken to S.S.M.
Hospital at Hassan, where he underwent a surgery and took treatment as an in-patient for one month and spent a sum of `5,00,000/- towards medical expenses.

The claimant has also stated that at the time of the accident, he was earning a sum of `25,000/- per month by doing agriculture and also milk vending business, however due to the injuries sustained in the road traffic accident, he is not in a position to the work as he was doing earlier.

With this,
holding the sole respondent -KSRTC, who is the owner-cum-insurer of the alleged offending Bus liable to pay him the compensation, the claimant claimed a compensation of a sum of `15,00,000/-
from the respondent -KSRTC with interest thereupon.

Raju A S vs The Divisional Controller on 23 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/21760595/
2 3.

entities.text: Raju A S vs The Divisional Controller
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In response to the Court notice served upon it before the Tribunal, the respondent - KSRTC appeared through its counsel and filed its statement of objections, wherein it not only denied the occurrence of the road traffic accident in the manner alleged by the claimant in his claim petition,
but also contended that the claimant himself rode the bike in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the KSRTC Bus, as such, it denied its liability to pay the compensation to the claimant.

4. Before the Tribunal, the claimant got himself examined as PW-1 and also examined Dr.
Vijaykumar A.V. as PW-2 and got marked documents from Exs.P-1 to P-74.

On behalf of the respondent - KSRTC, one Sri.R.D. Veerappa, an officer of the KSRTC was examined as RW-1,
however, no document was got marked.

5. After analysing the evidence and the materials placed before it, the Tribunal has awarded the compensation under the following heads with the sum shown against them:

and sufferings
3 Medical expenses 50,602-00  4 Conveyance, diet and attendant 15,000-00  charges  5 Loss of income during laid-up 21,000-00  period  Total 2,01,282-00 6.

The Tribunal has awarded a compensation of a sum of `2,01,282/- with interest at the rate of `9% per annum from the date of the claim petition till the date of deposit,
holding the respondent - KSRTC liable to pay the said compensation and directed it to deposit the award amount.
It is against the said judgment and award passed by the Tribunal, the claimant has filed this appeal seeking enhancement of compensation.
7. While filing this appeal, there was a delay of 121 days.

Thus, on an application - I.A.No.1/2019 filed by the learned counsel for appellant, this Court on the date 02-02-2022, has condoned the delay of 121 days in filing the appeal, denying the interest on the enhanced compensation, if any, for the said delayed period.

sentences.text: Records were called for from the Tribunal and the same are placed before the Court.
9. The learned counsel for the appellant (claimant) and the learned counsel for respondent- KSRTC are physically appearing before the Court.
10. Heard the arguments from both side.
Perused the materials placed before this Court including the memorandum of appeal, impugned judgment and also the records received from the Tribunal.

11. The present appeal being the claimant's appeal and the respondent KSRTC having not preferred either cross-objection or a counter appeal, the question of occurrence of the road traffic accident on the date, time and place as alleged by the claimant and also the alleged rash and negligent driving on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle Bus bearing registration No.KA-13/F- 2145 is not in dispute.

Further, the claimant, who got himself examined as PW-1, apart from reiterating the contentions taken up by him in his claim petition even in his examination-in-chief also, has also got produced documents from Exs.P-1 to P-7 which inter alia includes the copy of the FIR, complaint, charge sheet, wound certificate and Motor Vehicle Inspector's inspection report, which goes to establish the occurrence of the road traffic accident on the date, time and place as mentioned in the claim petition and the claimant sustaining injuries in the said accident, so also the rash and negligent driving on the part of the driver of the alleged offending Motor vehicle Bus bearing registration No.KA-13/F-2145 in causing the said road traffic accident and also the liability on the respondent KSRTC to compensate the claimant for the rash and negligent driving on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle Bus.
Thus, the only question that remains for consideration is, whether the claimant is entitled for any enhancement in the compensation awarded by the Tribunal in the matter.

12. The learned counsel for the appellant (claimant) in his argument submitted that, though the claimant did not produce any documents to establish his income at a sum of `25,000/- per month,
however, the Tribunal should have taken the notional income of the claimant at a sum of `9,000/-
per month, which was the prevailing notional income for the relevant year of the occurrence of the year of accident.
However, the Tribunal has taken only a sum of `7,000/- per month as the notional income of the claimant, as such, the same requires to be enhanced by this Court.

He further submitted that the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal towards pain and sufferings,
loss of income during the laid-up period and loss of future income is also on the lower side and requires to be enhanced.

13. Per contra, the learned counsel for the respondent - KSRTC, in her brief argument submitted that, the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal being just, fair and reasonable, does Raju A S vs The Divisional Controller on 23 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/21760595/
4 not warrant any interference at the hands of this Court.

entities.text: Raju A S vs The Divisional Controller on 23 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: She further submitted that, as per the order of this Court dated 02-02-2022, in case of enhancement of compensation, interest may be denied on the enhanced compensation for the delayed period of 121 days in filing this appeal.
14. In the road traffic accident, the claimant sustained multiple injuries which have been recorded in the wound certificate at Ex.P-4.
The said wound certificate goes to show that the claimant sustained lateral end - 10 - fracture of left clavicle, facial injury with left zygomatic arch, and blunt chest wall injury.
The Doctor has opined that the first two injuries were grievous in nature and the third injury was simple in nature.

According to the claimant, he has undergone a surgical operation towards the fracture sustained by him and was also treated as an in-patient in the Hospital, which, according to him, is for a period of one month.
Thus, considering the nature of the injuries suffered by him, the Tribunal has awarded a compensation of a sum of `50,000/- towards pain and sufferings.
The said quantum being reasonable, the same does not warrant any modification by this Court.

15. Even though the complainant (claimant) has claimed in his petition and in his evidence that, he has spent a sum of `5,00,000/- towards the medical expenses, but the medical bills and prescriptions produced by him and marked as exhibits from Exs.P-7 to P-71 would only to go to show that, he has incurred an expenditure only to an extent of `50,602/-.
It is based on the actuals since the - 11 - Tribunal has awarded the said amount as compensation towards the medical expenses, the same does not warrant any modification in it.
16. Towards conveyance, diet and attendant charges, the Tribunal has awarded a compensation of a sum of `15,000/-.

The said quantum being reasonable, in the facts and circumstances of the case,
the same quantum is retained without any modification.

17. The claimant has contended in his evidence as PW-1 that, at the time of the road traffic accident,
he was working as an agriculturist and also doing milk vending business and earning a sum of `25,000-/- per month.
Admittedly, he has not produced any document to corroborate his evidence.
The respondent - KSRTC has denied his alleged income.
As such, though the Tribunal has rightly decided to take the notional income of the claimant, however, in the said process, it has taken his notional income at a sum of `7,000/- per month.

Since the notional income prevailing in the year 2015 and being - 12 - Raju A S vs The Divisional Controller on 23 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/21760595/
5 taken by a large number of Motor Accident claims Tribunals in the State for the relevant period was `9,000/- per month, even in the instant case also, the same quantum is required to be taken.

entities.text: Raju A S vs The Divisional Controller
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Thus,
when the income of the claimant is taken at a sum of `9,000/- per month, the compensation towards loss of income during laid-up period, which is computed by the Tribunal at the rate of `7,000/- per month, for three months at `21,000/-, deserves enhancement by a differential amount of a sum of `6,000/- [i.e.`9,000/-x3 months =`27,000/- (-) `21,000/-].
18.
The claimant has stated in his evidence that at the time of the road traffic accident, his age was 50 years, however, the medical records has shown his age as 55 years.
On the other hand, a copy of the Learner's licence produced by the claimant before the Tribunal has shown his age as 51 years.
As such, rightly the Tribunal has considered his age as 51 years, as at the time of the road - 13 - traffic accident.
The proper multiplier applicable for the said age is '11'.

The claimant has contended that due to the injuries suffered by him in the road traffic accident, he has suffered permanent disability and is unable to continue his work as he was doing prior to the date of accident.
In that regard, he got examined one Dr. Vijaykumar A.V. as PW-2.

The said Doctor has stated that he is not a treating Doctor, however, he has stated that, the treating Doctor of the claimant, i.e. Dr. Gangu Hiral, since had been to abroad and was not available, based on the documents maintained in the Hospital, he is giving the evidence on his behalf.
The said witness (PW-2) has stated that, considering the injuries suffered by the claimant, the disability can be calculated at 22% with respect to the left hand.

In his cross-examination, nothing much could be elicited which was beneficial to the respondent-KSRTC, as such, based on the said evidence of the Doctor assessing the percentage of disability to one of the particular hand at - 14 - 22%, the Tribunal has rightly considered the disability applicable to the whole body at 7%.

In the light of the enhancement made in the notional income for the claimant, the quantum of the compensation towards future loss of income requires recalculation which comes to a sum of `83,160/- (i.e.`9,000/- x 12 months x '11' multiplier x 7/100).

After deducting a sum of `64,680/-
awarded by the Tribunal
, the claimant (appellant) is entitled for the differential amount of `18,480/- as enhancement under this head.

19. From the nature of injuries suffered by the claimant which were in the form of fracture of left clavicle and fracture of left zygomatic arch, it is clear that the claimant is unable to enjoy the amenities and comforts in life to the fullest extent, as such, towards loss of amenities and comforts in life, the claimant deserves to be awarded some compensation.
However, the Tribunal has not considered to grant any compensation under the said head to the claimant.

Thus, the claimant is entitled for a sum of - 15 - Raju A S vs The Divisional Controller on 23 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/21760595/
6 `20,000/- towards the loss of amenities and comforts in life.
20.

Since the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal at a sum of `2,01,282/-
is in short by a sum of `44,480/-, for the said enhancement of a sum of `44,480/-
only, the impugned judgment and award deserves to be interfered with.

- 16 - Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following :
ORDER [i] The appeal filed by the claimant stands allowed in part;
[ii] The impugned judgment and award passed by the learned Senior Civil Judge and Motor Accident Claims Tribunal at Holenarasipur, dated 30-03-2019, in M.V.C.No.578/2016, is hereby modified to the extent that the compensation awarded at `2,01,282/- is enhanced by a sum of `44,480/- (Rupees Forty Four Thousand Four Hundred and Eighty only), thus fixing the total compensation at `2,45,762/- (Rupees Two Lakhs Forty Five Thousand Seven Hundred and Sixty Two only).

However, since while condoning the delay of 121 days caused in filing this appeal, in view of the order of this Court dated 02-02-2022 passed on I.A.No.1/2019, the claimant is not entitled to interest on the enhanced compensation of `44,480/- for a period of 121 days.
